title: Automating evaluation: test sets and unit tests on output

videos.script: A test set is a list of messages, each with the answer a person decided was right. Every number in this course so far was counted against one. {{title}} This lesson is about the set itself, and about the ways its count can mislead you. {{set}} Each check in the harness is a unit test on one reply. Does it parse, does it have the fields, are the labels legal, does it match the person. The cheap checks run first. {{checks}} Then you meet the easy set. The prompt that passes twenty-eight of forty messages its author wrote passes fourteen of thirty harder ones, written later. {{holdout}} Next you copy three failing test messages into the prompt as its examples. The total does not move, the categories look nearly solved, and on the harder set the score falls from fourteen to nine. {{contamination}} Last, you raise the temperature. Two runs differ by one message, which is the size of difference prompts are compared on. Five samples per message show which failures are stable and which are a rate. {{flaky}} By the end you can build a set that keeps measuring, and report a number that survives the next run. {{close}}
